record.name: Canadian AI Safety Institute
record.host: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
record.mandate: Researches risks from advanced AI systems and develops measures to address them.

funding.annual_basis: Arithmetic mean of the explicitly stated CAD 50m five-year allocation; annual disbursements and spending are not stated. Budget 2024 chapter 4 gives a yearly profile only for the combined Safe and Responsible Use of AI measures, not a separate institute profile.

funding.description: An additional CAD 50m announced through AI for All to expand CAISI capabilities.
funding.notes: The retrieved sources publish no funding period or annual profile, so we do not annualise it, do not use it in place of the 2024 five-year allocation, and do not add the two envelopes to a current annual budget. The one-off label denotes this additional fixed envelope, not payment in one fiscal year. The strategy names CAISI as the recipient, and the Question Period Note explicitly calls this additional funding. It is an institute-wide envelope, kept separate from the earlier five-year allocation rather than added to its annual mean. The Question Period Note also associates the envelope with AI transparency and a Canada Trusted AI Certification programme. It gives no split; the explicit CAISI allocation supports the whole-institute classification while the scope of certification spending remains uncertain.

funding.period: 2024-25 to 2028-29 (2024-25 and 2025-26 actual spending, later years planned spending)
funding.description: Contributions to CIFAR for CAISI's applied and investigator-led research stream, 2024-25 to 2028-29: CAD 2,999,545 actual spending in 2024-25 (funding received in-year, none planned), CAD 6m actual spending in 2025-26 and CAD 6m planned for each later year.
funding.annual_basis: Planned contribution for 2026-27, the fiscal year containing the dataset date, in ISED's 2026-27 Departmental Plan; planned spending, not expenditure. One research stream only.
funding.notes: ISED's 2026-27 Departmental Plan lists the CAISI project under the Advanced and Emerging Technology programme with a start of 2024-25 and an end of 2028-29 (CAISI Budget 2024), as does its 2025-26 results report, so this stream sits inside the CAD 50m five-year allocation and is not additional to it. ISED's 2024-25 results report and its 2025-26 Departmental Plan give the start as 2025-26, but the 2024-25 results report also records CAD 2,999,545 of actual spending in 2024-25 against nothing planned, as funding received in-year, and says the stream was launched in November 2024; the record therefore starts in 2024-25. ISED's 2025-26 Departmental Results Report gives CAD 6m as 2025-26 actual spending (authorities used), equal to planned spending. CIFAR reported on 21 January 2026 that the government awarded it CAD 27m through the institute for its AI safety research programme, with no period stated, and that the programme awarded CAD 2.4m in 2025 to 12 projects; both concern this stream and are not added to it.

testing_capacity.notes: Function statement, not counted as testing: 'We conduct projects supporting the government's priorities on AI safety, including joint testing with international counterparts' (ISED institute page). ISED says the institute 'directly conducts projects supporting the Government's priorities on AI safety through the National Research Council', a stream 'implemented through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the National Research Council (NRC)'. The National Research Council says its researchers took part in a joint testing exercise through the institute, evaluating AI agents and how well AI prevents harmful content in nine languages. No headcount or technical staff is published. Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise) and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise); the network reports credit Canada with analysis. The renewed UK-Canada partnership of 13 October 2026 mentions 'exploring staff exchanges and coordinated evaluation activities'. The national AI strategy says Canada will invest $50 million to expand the institute's capabilities, including to conduct transparent evaluations of AI models.

model_access.notes: No access event, legal power or agreement providing for access to, or evaluation of, the models of a developer that has a model in Epoch AI's frontier set was found. Under the Cohere MOU of June 2025 'Cohere will collaborate with the Canadian AI Safety Institute'; no access term was retrieved, and Cohere has no model in Epoch AI's frontier set. No statute gives the institute access powers.
